Senses.Explanation: Literally a rule, standard, or code. Across 3,110 occurrences in 360 allowlisted texts, it names ordained regulation, its specialists, regulated conduct, and the rules cited in public interview. The Platform Record’s ordination account distinguishes the Vinaya-master roles: Zhiguang bestows the precepts, Huijing conducts the formal act, Tongying instructs, and Jiduoluo recites the precepts. A master who declines an expected address says, ‘scriptures have scripture masters; rules have Vinaya masters’ (經有經師，律有律師), while another exchange begins, ‘the code says that hearing ornaments through a wall is called breaking the precepts’ (律中道。隔壁聞釵釧聲即名破戒) and then asks whether a crowded visual scene is or is not precept-breaking. The Baizhang account records a specifically Chan institutional bend: asked why he did not simply follow an existing greater-vehicle precept code, he says his tradition is neither confined to nor different from the greater and lesser vehicles, calls for standards fitted to circumstances, and establishes a separate Chan residence. The Record of the Source-Mirror says, ‘all one’s doings enter regulated conduct’ (所有施為，皆入律行). Yongjue also records and rebukes the dismissal, ‘holding and breaking are originally absent—what use are precepts and code?’ (本無持犯，何用戒律？). The headword therefore remains concrete code-language while Chan records assign it offices, cite it in interview, fit communal standards to circumstances, extend it to conduct, and preserve arguments over its cancellation.
Senses.Note: Flyswatter-test deviation: code-language is not excluded as generic Buddhism; the Baizhang record deploys it in the founding description of a separate Chan residence. Exact count: 3,110 hits in 360 files.

Occurrences.Kwic: 西京智光律師為授戒師，蘇州慧靜律師為羯磨，荊州通應律師為教授，中天耆多羅律師為說戒，西國蜜多三藏為證戒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Record distinguishes the formal offices at Huineng’s ordination.

Occurrences.Kwic: 或曰。瑜伽論瓔珞經。是大乘戒律。胡不依隨哉。師曰。吾所宗非局大小乘。非異大小乘。當博約折中設於制範務其宜也。於是創意別立禪居。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Asked why he does not follow the greater-vehicle precept code, Baizhang says rules are fitted to circumstances and a separate Chan residence is established.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所有施為。皆入律行。自然成辦一切佛事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of the Source-Mirror says all doings enter regulated conduct.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: After declining an expected address, a master distinguishes scripture and rule specialists.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public exchange cites the code's boundary and asks whether a second scene is precept-breaking.

Occurrences.Kwic: 本無持犯，何用戒律？因果罪福，一切滅裂。至於貪名奪利，有如狂狗；恃氣起爭，不啻猛虎。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjue quotes and rebukes the claim that precepts and code are useless because holding and breaking are originally absent.

Senses.Explanation: In the compound (音律), (律) denotes regulated sound, meter, or tonal pattern rather than a monastic code. A Chan verse says that an old tune is not reducible to musical regulation before turning to the South Mountain turtle-nosed snake; two major lamp compilations preserve that deployment. Modern scholarly body prose in the allowlisted corpus likewise judges a song's musical regulation sound while rejecting its wording. The shared object is ordering of sound, not ordained conduct.
Senses.Note: This is a different referent from Vinaya or communal code. C077 and C078 preserve related recensions of one Chan verse; B25n0143 supplies an independent body-prose witness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打皷弄琵琶相逢一會家雲門能合調長慶解隨邪古曲非音律南山鼈鼻蛇何人知妙訣
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A Chan verse moves from drum, lute, and matching the mode to the claim that the old tune is not musical regulation, then raises the turtle-nosed snake.

Occurrences.Kwic: 打鼓弄琵琶相逢一會家雲門能合調長慶觧隨邪古曲非音律南山鼈鼻蛇何人知妙訣
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A second lamp compilation preserves the same sound-and-mode verse, anchoring the headword “regulation” (律) inside “musical regulation” (音律).

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然「音律不差」，而「下語用字，全不可讀」，也沒有文學價值
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Allowlisted modern scholarly body prose distinguishes acceptable musical regulation from unreadable wording.

Senses.Explanation: A title for a specialist and teacher in the monastic rule code. The term occurs 407 times in 114 allowlisted texts. Chan biographies use it straightforwardly for ordination teachers, as when Huairang leaves home under Vinaya Master Hongjing. An early account places Vinaya Master Guangtong and the translator Bodhiruci in sustained dispute with Bodhidharma after they see him reject appearances and point to mind. Public cases also use the office as an interlocutor and a contrast. Vinaya Master Yuan asks Dazhu whether he uses effort in the way; after Dazhu answers with eating when hungry and sleeping when tired, Yuan falls silent. In Yaoshan's refusal to speak after the assembly gathers, Yaoshan says, 'Scriptures have scripture masters, treatises have treatise masters, and rules have Vinaya masters—how can you blame this old monk?' The Zen bend lies in those public deployments: the recognized rules specialist is brought into debate and interview, and the office may be named as the specialist role against which a Chan master declines an expected lecture. It is a foil only in those attested exchanges, not by definition everywhere.
Senses.Note: The title is translated by office. Biographical honorific uses remain ordinary; the explanation restricts the foil claim to quoted encounters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 依弘景律師出家通天二年受戒後習毘尼藏
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A biography names Vinaya Master Hongjing as the teacher under whom Huairang left home.

Occurrences.Kwic: 源律師問：和尚修道，還用功否？師曰：用功。曰：如何用功？師曰：飢來喫飯，困來即眠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Vinaya Master Yuan publicly questions Dazhu about using effort; the exchange supplies the office-holder's foil role.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：經有經師，律有律師，爭怪得老僧？丹霞天然禪師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yaoshan lists scripture, treatise, and Vinaya specialists after declining to deliver the expected address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 光統律師流支三藏者乃僧中之鸞鳳也。覩師演道斥相指心。每與師論議是非鋒起。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An early transmission account says Vinaya Master Guangtong and Bodhiruci repeatedly argued right and wrong with Bodhidharma after hearing him reject appearances and point to mind.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, Wang, old master or teacher. In the Chan record this is Nanquan Puyuan's recurrent self-designation and the label later writers use when quoting or commenting on him. The compound occurs 760 times in 193 allowlisted texts. Nanquan's biography identifies him as Puyuan, a son of the Wang family of Zhengzhou, and immediately records him saying, 'Old Master Wang is selling himself; is there anyone who will buy?' Other self-references include the water-buffalo saying, 'Old Master Wang has raised a water buffalo since he was young,' asking Zhaozhou, 'Where is Old Master Wang at fault?' and saying that Old Master Wang, unlike Mazu, does not say 'mind is buddha' but 'not mind, not buddha, not a thing.' Later comments preserve the title while explicitly naming Nanquan.
Senses.Note: This is a person-title, not a generic entry for every teacher surnamed Wang. The explicit biography and repeated Nanquan section headings fix its principal referent. The full name 'Nanquan Old Master Wang' occurs 17 times in 12 texts; the selling-himself phrase occurs 41 times in 37.

Occurrences.Kwic: 二密古尊宿語錄卷第十三勿一南泉禪師語錄馬祖大寂禪師法嗣。南泉禪師諱普願鄭州王氏子也示眾云王老師賣身去也還有人買麼時有僧出眾云某甲買師云不
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Nanquan record identifies Puyuan as a son of the Wang family and immediately preserves his selling-himself saying.

Occurrences.Kwic: 泉進且無路，退亦無門。良久，云：別處容和尚不得。示眾云：王老師自小養一頭水牯牛，擬向溪東牧，不免食他國王水草；擬向溪西牧，不免食他國王
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Within Nanquan Puyuan's section, the master says that Old Master Wang has raised a water buffalo since youth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 與二十棒，趂出院去也。時趙州出眾曰：和尚棒教誰喫？泉曰：王老師過在什麼處？州便禮拜而出。雲門偃云：深領和尚慈悲，某甲歸衣鉢下，得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the two-halls cat case, Nanquan asks Zhaozhou where Old Master Wang is at fault; later commentary follows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欄頻顧望，回首與誰同？南泉示眾云：江西馬大師說即心即佛，王老師不恁麼，不是心，不是佛，不是物。恁麼道還有過麼？鼓山珪頌云：剔
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A collected record explicitly identifies Nanquan before his contrast between Mazu's wording and Old Master Wang's wording.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉似南泉，泉曰：苦哉！浮盃被者老婆摧折一上。婆聞，笑曰：王老師猶少機關在。澄一禪客見婆，乃問：怎生是南泉猶少機關在？婆哭曰：可悲
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a reported exchange, an old woman hears Nanquan's response and says that Old Master Wang still lacks a turn of mechanism.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覺云：遇水喫水，遇草喫草，焉知畜生行？示眾云：諸和尚子！王老師十八上便解作活計，如今莫有解作活計底麼？出來共汝商量。良久，顧
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Nanquan tells the assembly that Old Master Wang already knew how to manage the affair at eighteen.

Senses.Explanation: Literally (見) 'see' + (性) 'nature': to see one's own nature. It is the operative half of the four-phrase slogan that defines the Chan school — (教外別傳)，(不立文字)，(直指人心)，(見性成佛) ('a separate transmission outside the teachings; not setting up words; pointing straight at the human mind; seeing [one's] nature and becoming Buddha') — and recurs in the near-synonyms (明心見性) ('clarify the mind and see nature') and (識心見性) ('know the mind and see nature'), the latter being what Zhaozhou calls 'the road that does not go wrong.' In the Bodhidharma-cycle case of the heretic-king (異見王), the venerable Boluoti (波羅提) says (見性是佛), 'seeing nature is Buddha.' A monk brings Xuefeng the canonical grading (a śrāvaka sees nature 'as one sees the moon at night,' a bodhisattva 'as one sees the sun by day'), and Xuefeng answers with three blows (打三下). Guizong says even (悟明見性) ('awakening and seeing nature') is (錯用心) ('misusing the mind'). Render it literally as 'see [one's] nature,' following the plain reading of (見性成佛) as 'see nature, become Buddha.' An in-corpus definition survives as a case: asked (如何是見性) (itself a live test-question, 15 hits in 13 allowlist texts), the master answers (性即是見)，(見即是性)，(不可以性更見性)；(聞即是性)，(不可以性更聞性) (nature is precisely seeing, seeing is precisely nature; one cannot see nature by means of nature again — 天聖廣燈錄 X78n1553; parallel 古尊宿語錄 C077n1710), and (五燈會元續略) carries the same definition credited to (大顛): (僧問大顛)：(如何是見性)？(顛曰)：(見即是性) (X80n1566). (傳燈玉英集) states (見性者即非凡夫頓悟上乘超凡越聖) (one who sees nature is no ordinary man — sudden awakening to the higher vehicle, beyond the ordinary and beyond the holy) and (若見性者號之為佛) (if one sees nature he is titled a Buddha) (B14n0082). Other recorded answers to the question do not define at all: asked (如何是見性明心之旨), a master answers (快煎茶來)，(與雷居士喫) (quick — brew tea for layman Lei; J39nB466). The Jingde-era lamp record preserves another direct definition in the exchange of Tiantai Yunju Zhi: 'one has never seen; when the place and form of seeing cannot be obtained, the one able to see and what is seen are both cut off; this is called seeing nature' (未嘗見。求見處體相不可得。能所俱絕。名為見性). Parallel recensions carry the same exchange in the Chan Gate Treasury Record (禪門寶藏錄), the Combined Essentials of the Five Lamps (聯燈會要), and later lamp compilations.
Senses.Note: Very widely attested: (見性) has 2,148 occurrences across 304 allowlist texts. The exact unpunctuated sequence (直指人心見性成佛) appears 63 times in 29 texts, while (直指人心) alone has 624 hits in 216 texts. Collocation counts: (見性成佛) 684 hits/213 texts, (明心見性) 146/84, (識心見性) 39/24, (見性是佛) 37/34. Curated occurrences span the slogan, the (見性是佛) case, Zhaozhou, Xuefeng's three blows to the monk's moon/sun grading, and Guizong's (錯用心) line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 佛法有教外別傳、不立文字、直指人心、見性成佛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The school's four-phrase self-definition, here in the Linji record (臨濟錄).

Occurrences.Kwic: 『何者是佛？』提曰：『見性是佛。』王曰：『師見性否？』提曰：『我見佛性。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Quoted case of the venerable Boluoti (波羅提尊者) answering the heretic-king (異見王): (見性是佛), 'seeing nature is Buddha.' (Boluoti is the venerable who converts 異見王 in the Bodhidharma cycle; not Prajnatara/般若多羅 and not a patriarch.)

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是不錯路？師云：識心見性是不錯路。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhaozhou: 'knowing the mind and seeing nature is the road that does not go wrong.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問雪峰：『聲聞人見性如夜見月，菩薩人見性如晝見日。未審和尚見性如何？』峰打三下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The monk grades seeing-nature (moon-at-night vs sun-by-day); Xuefeng answers with three blows (打三下).

Occurrences.Kwic: 歸宗和尚道：『參學人，切忌錯用心。悟明見性，是錯用心；成佛作祖，是錯用心；
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Guizong: even (悟明見性) ('awakening and seeing nature') is (錯用心) ('misusing the mind').

Occurrences.Kwic: 未嘗見。求見處體相不可得。能所俱絕。名為見性。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde-era Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in Tiantai Yunju Zhi's exchange with the Huayan-cloister monk Jizong: 'one has never seen; when the place and form of seeing cannot be obtained, the one able to see and what is seen are both cut off; this is called seeing nature' (未嘗見。求見處體相不可得。能所俱絕。名為見性).

AlternateTargets: see the nature and become a Buddha
Senses.Explanation: (見) 'see' + (性) 'nature' + (成佛) 'become Buddha': the claim that awakening is seeing one's own (Buddha-)nature, and that in that seeing one becomes Buddha. It is the culminating clause of the four-phrase slogan by which the Chan school defines itself — (教外別傳)，(不立文字)，(直指人心)，(見性成佛) ('a separate transmission outside the teachings; not setting up words; pointing straight at the human mind; seeing [one's] nature and becoming Buddha') — and appears as the Southern school's slogan, the teaching Yaoshan reports hearing of ('甞聞南方直指人心。見性成佛。實未明了'). When a master glosses it, the gloss is equational: the venerable of Yunju answers (繼宗)'s question 'what does (見性成佛) mean?' with (性即佛)。(佛即性)。(故曰見性成佛) ('the nature is just Buddha, Buddha is just the nature; therefore it is called seeing-nature-becoming-Buddha'). One hall-discourse makes it the whole of the matter — (祖師西來只道見性成佛)。(其餘所說不及此說) ('the Patriarch came from the West only to say see-nature-become-Buddha; nothing else said measures up'). A second in-corpus self-definition appears in (續燈正統): (天奇本瑞), opening an instruction with (祖師西來)，(不立文字)，(直指人心)，(見性成佛)，(更無別法) ('…there is no other teaching'), states (須知所謂見性成佛者)，(見性不是見他人之性)，(成佛不是成他人之佛)，(決定是汝諸人本有之性) ('know that in what is called seeing-the-nature-becoming-Buddha, the seeing of the nature is not seeing someone else's nature, and the becoming Buddha is not becoming someone else's Buddha: it is decidedly the nature you all inherently have'), adding (人人本具)，(箇箇不無) ('each person inherently equipped with it, not one without it'). (遠菴僼禪師語錄) answers the question form directly: (何謂直指人心)、(見性成佛者)？(不教人千劫學威儀)、(萬劫修相好)，(只要人於善知識一言一句下)，(頓脫無始結使纏縛) ('what is meant by pointing straight at the human mind, seeing the nature and becoming Buddha? It does not have people study deportment for a thousand kalpas or refine the marks for ten thousand kalpas; it only wants a person, at one word or phrase from a good teacher, to suddenly cast off the beginningless bonds and fetters'). Render it literally as 'see [one's] nature, become Buddha'. It CONTAINS (見性) ('seeing nature', its own entry): (見性成佛) is (見性) with its consequence (成佛) stated — keep the two distinct but cross-referenced.
Senses.Note: Very widely attested (approximately 684 raw occurrences across 213 allowlist texts, independent strict count; an earlier tally of 602/206 did not reproduce); the four-clause (直指人心見性成佛) formula alone is pervasive. Uniform meaning across the corpus — a shared banner/topic, not a master-specific coinage — so one corpus-wide sense is honest. Curated witnesses span three independent texts: (六祖大師法寶壇經) (T48n2008, Huineng), (五燈會元) (X80n1565, the Yunju gloss and the Yaoshan report), and (景德傳燈錄) (T51n2076). Per the nested-term rule (§5b): (見性成佛) CONTAINS the standalone entry (見性); both kept as separate entries and cross-referenced in RelatedTerms, not merged. Slogan-family counts (Zen-scoped): the contiguous (直指人心見性成佛) 63x/29 texts; companions (直指人心) 624x/216, (教外別傳) 640x/211, (不立文字) 435x/188; the contained (見性) 2,148x/304. The (天奇本瑞) self-definition: X84n1583 (續燈正統) ed="X" lb 0571a06; the (遠菴僼) answer: J37nB386 lb 0403c22.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃名見性。性即佛。佛即性。故曰見性成佛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元) (X-canon; FromLb is the ed="X" number): (天台山雲居智禪師) answering the monk (繼宗)'s question 'what does (見性成佛) mean?' — 'the nature is just Buddha, Buddha is just the nature; therefore it is called see-nature-become-Buddha.' The equational gloss. Two-speaker exchange; the answer is the master's, but MasterName left null (雲居智 not a confirmed canonical master name).

Occurrences.Kwic: 普願法界眾生，言下見性成佛。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (六祖大師法寶壇經): Huineng preaching at the (大梵寺) — 'I universally wish that beings throughout the whole realm see their nature and become Buddha at [these] words.' The founding text's use of the phrase in the Patriarch's own voice.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖師西來只道見性成佛。其餘所說不及此說。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄), in a hall-discourse: 'the Patriarch came from the West only to say see-nature-become-Buddha; nothing else said measures up to this saying.' Independent witness making the phrase the whole of the matter. Governing section head is (廬山歸宗第十四世慧誠禪師) (Guizong Huicheng); not a rostered master, so MasterName null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 甞聞南方直指人心。見性成佛。實未明了。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元): Yaoshan (藥山) to Shitou (石頭) — 'I have heard that in the South they point straight at the human mind, see nature and become Buddha, but I truly have not understood it.' The four-clause slogan reported as a known Southern teaching. Two-speaker exchange, MasterName null. FromLb is the ed="X" number.

Occurrences.Kwic: 須知所謂見性成佛者，見性不是見他人之性，成佛不是成他人之佛，決定是汝諸人本有之性
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (續燈正統) (X-canon; FromLb is the ed="X" number), section (安陸府荊門州天奇本瑞禪師) (cb:mulu; 大鑑下第三十世, 寶峰瑄禪師法嗣): the master's own instruction after taking an abbacy (住後落堂，開示) — the fullest in-corpus self-definition of the phrase: the nature seen is not another's nature, the Buddha become is not another's Buddha.

AlternateTargets: what one sees, hears, senses, and knows
Senses.Explanation: The four ordinary functions of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, named together as a fixed sequence. Chan texts warn against constructing an additional understanding from them or treating some separate entity as standing behind them. The same functions can be described as the cause of birth and death and, without changing the wording, as the root of release. Other passages say that they neither obstruct complete command nor bind a person in themselves. Translate the four actions directly; do not replace them with an imported technical noun such as 'awareness.'
Senses.Note: The corpus has 787 matches in 162 files. Sixty-six matches in forty-six files occur in constructions about leaving or being apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. Five passages in five files use the explicit nominal form 'as for seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing,' and three in three use 'the so-called seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing.' The corrective passages show that the compound names the four functions themselves, not a separate faculty.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大德若作見聞覺知之解。與道懸殊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teacher says, 'Worthy ones, if you make an understanding out of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, it is far removed from the Way.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 見聞覺知俱為生死之因，見聞覺知正是解脫之本。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The text sets two descriptions side by side: seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are all the cause of birth and death; seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are precisely the root of release.

Occurrences.Kwic: 見聞覺知無障礙聲香味觸常三昧
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse says, 'Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing have no obstruction; sounds, scents, flavors, and contacts are constant complete command.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 心法本來是見是聞是覺是知。不應於見聞覺知上別有所謂見聞覺知者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng says, 'The activity of mind is originally seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. One should not set up some separate so-called seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing on top of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 不被見聞覺知所縛。不被諸境所惑。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A record says, 'Not bound by seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing; not confused by the various scenes.'

Senses.PreferredTarget: open your mouth and you are already wrong
AlternateTargets: the moment you open your mouth, it is wrong
Senses.Explanation: Literally, open (開) the mouth (口) and immediately or already (即) be wrong (錯): "open your mouth and you are already wrong." The phrase occurs 43 times in 34 allowlisted texts; the variant "open your mouth and it is then wrong" (開口便錯) occurs 13 times in 10. Its early defining exchange has a monk ask Dabe to speak apart from removing the upper and taking away the lower. Dabe answers, "when I open my mouth I am already wrong" (我開口即錯). The monk calls him truly his teacher; Dabe replies, "today I died in the disciple's hands" (今日向弟子手裏死), so the record shows the verdict catching the speaker's own utterance. Later masters make it a portable paired formula: Po'an says, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; aim the mind and you immediately miss" (開口即錯，擬心即差). Other records pair it with "move a thought and immediately go against" (動念即乖). Wuzhun states the closed-mouth counterpart, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; close your mouth and you are already lost," then asks how communication is possible apart from opening and not opening (開口即錯，閉口即喪，不開不合，十萬八千). The phrase also becomes an encounter instruction: Baishan tells a monk, "open your mouth and you are already wrong; move a thought and immediately go against; leave these two roads and speak quickly!" The monk answers, "wrong," and Baishan answers with another stock retort. Chan thus bends an ordinary judgment of erroneous speech into a self-applying verdict, a fixed parallel line, and a demand used while requiring an answer; the records preserve the resulting replies rather than defining silence as the solution.
Senses.Note: The exact phrase is not a ban on all recorded speech: masters utter it, ask for rapid answers after it, pair it with closed-mouth loss, and continue the exchange. Those observable deployments are why the preferred target preserves the self-applying grammar.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有僧問。除上去下請師便道。師曰。我開口即錯。僧曰。真是學人師。師曰。今日向弟子手裏死。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dabe's early exchange makes the line explicitly first-person and records his acknowledgment that the disciple caught him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 開口即錯，擬心即差
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Po'an Zuxian preserves the fixed parallel with aiming the mind and immediately missing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 開口即錯，閉口即喪。不開不合，十萬八千。到這裏如何通信？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuzhun Shifan supplies the closed-mouth contrast and then asks how communication is possible.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：「開口即錯，動念即乖。去此二途，速道！速道！」曰：「錯。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baishan demands a rapid answer after stating the paired verdict; the monk replies with the word 'wrong.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 問僧，開口即錯，閉口即失。去此二途，如何通信？僧曰，兩眼對兩眼。師曰，瞎。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanzhi Benyuan tests a monk with opening-mouth error versus closed-mouth loss and rejects the reply 'two eyes facing two eyes' as blind.

Senses.Explanation: (開) 'open' + (悟) 'awaken/realize': to open into awakening — the event of a person coming to realization. In the Chan record it names the moment understanding opens, most often marked as sudden and triggered by a teacher's word or gesture: (豁然開悟) ('all at once opened into awakening'), (心忽開悟) ('the mind suddenly opened into awakening'), (遇百丈開悟) ('met Baizhang and opened into awakening'), (其僧於是開悟) ('the monk thereupon opened into awakening'). Yongming reads the opening as instantaneous — (若開悟時)，(不隔剎那)，(便成佛果) ('when one opens into awakening, not a kṣaṇa apart, one accomplishes the fruit of Buddhahood'). The same word is also used transitively/causatively — (令汝等開悟) ('to make you all open into awakening'), (開悟眾生) — with no change of core meaning, only of who does the awakening. Distinguish (大悟) (great awakening, esp. the stock 言下大悟 'greatly awakened at the words') and (頓悟) (sudden awakening), which name the same event under different emphasis; (見性成佛) names its content. The corpus's own collocation pattern draws that line: the words-trigger formula (言下) pairs almost exclusively with (大悟) (言下大悟 450 hits in 148 allowlist texts, against 言下開悟 4 hits), while (開悟) takes the suddenness adverbs — (豁然開悟) 68 hits in 38 texts, (忽然開悟) 18 in 16.
Senses.Note: Very widely attested (566 raw occurrences across 147 allowlist texts). Uniform core meaning; no master bends it, so a single corpus-wide sense is honest. The intransitive 'X opened into awakening' is dominant; a transitive-causative valence ('to open others to awakening', 令汝等開悟 / 開悟眾生, especially in Yongming's 宗鏡錄 and Mazu's address to the assembly) is the same lexical sense and is documented in the occurrences. Curated witnesses span three independent texts: (景德傳燈錄) (T51n2076), (五燈會元) (X80n1565), and (宗鏡錄) (T48n2016). Collocation counts (462-text allowlist grep): (豁然開悟) 68 hits in 38 texts; (忽然開悟) 18 in 16; (言下開悟) 4 in 3 — versus (言下大悟) 450 in 148 and (豁然大悟) 353 in 126; the transitive (開悟眾生) 3 in 2.

Occurrences.Kwic: 行脚遇百丈開悟。却迴本寺。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄) narration of (福州古靈神贊禪師): on pilgrimage he 'met Baizhang and opened into awakening,' then returned to his home temple. Narrator's voice, not the master speaking — MasterName null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 殃崛聞之。心忽開悟。遂棄刃。投佛出家。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元) (X-canon; FromLb is the ed="X" number, not the co-located ed="R138" reprint): Aṅgulimāla, hearing the Buddha, 'the mind suddenly opened into awakening,' cast down the blade and left home. Independent witness of the intransitive event.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若開悟時。不隔剎那。便成佛果。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (宗鏡錄), Yongming Yanshou: awakening is instantaneous — 'when one opens into awakening, not a kṣaṇa apart, one accomplishes the fruit of Buddhahood.' The non-gradual, instantaneous reading.

Occurrences.Kwic: 傳上乘一心之法。令汝等開悟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (五燈會元), (馬祖道一) addressing his assembly (謂眾曰) and describing Bodhidharma: '[Bodhidharma] transmitted the highest-vehicle teaching of the one mind to make you all open into awakening.' Documents the transitive-causative valence ('to open others to awakening'). Speaker is Mazu (expository/two-speaker), MasterName null. FromLb is the ed="X" number.

Occurrences.Kwic: 搖三五下作蟬響聲。其僧於是開悟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄): a master mimics a cicada's cry and 'the monk thereupon opened into awakening' — the event triggered by a gesture. Two-speaker narration, MasterName null.

Senses.Explanation: Literally to open and show: to disclose something or give a showing. In Chan public interviews an assembly or monk asks a master to disclose and show, and the master's spoken reply follows. One monk asks for the intention of the patriarch's coming from the west and receives “the mud ox swallows the huge wave”; another assembly asks and receives a verse about clouds and snow. In the Longtan–Tianhuang case, Longtan complains that he has long attended without being shown the essentials of mind. Tianhuang lists raising a hand when tea was brought and lowering his head when greeted, then asks, “where was I not showing you the essentials of mind?” (那裏不是與你開示心要處). Biographical prose also says a teacher used a responsive dynamic to “show later students” (開示後學). A later speaker says, “having received the master's disclosure” (承師開示), treating the reply as instruction already given. Request, act, repeated conduct, and received instruction are stages of the same showing, not different lexical referents.
Senses.Note: The term occurs 1,446 times in 267 allowlisted texts. The former verb/result targets were request and receipt grammar for the same showing and are merged. Compare raising and expounding (舉揚), question-and-answer (問答), offering an indication (垂示), addressing the assembly (示眾), and formal instruction words (法語). No mystical content is assigned to the act or its received result.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：祖意西來，願垂開示。師曰：泥牛吞巨浪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A public question requests disclosure and receives a recorded answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：大眾雲臻，請師開示。師曰：又靜不知雲去處，地寒留得雪多時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An assembled audience requests the master's public showing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今日福山大眾請和尚開示
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A named assembly's request is immediately followed by the master's answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我既得法。當往何國而作佛事。願垂開示。尊者曰。汝雖得法未可遠遊。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A transmission narrative uses the same polite request formula and supplies an answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「承師開示，腳底蓮花步步階。」師云：「一法通時萬法通。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker treats the master's disclosure as instruction already received, then continues the exchange.

Occurrences.Kwic: 學人久依和尚。不蒙開示心要。皇曰。你擎茶來我則舉手。你來問訊我則低頭。那裏不是與你開示心要處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Longtan complains that he has not been shown the essentials of mind; Tianhuang lists his responses to tea and greetings and asks where he was not showing them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 常以啐啄之機。開示後學。善能應機說法。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Biographical prose says Jingqing regularly used the hatching dynamic to show later students and was skilled at responding to the situation in speech.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'opening and blocking': in precept language, permission and prohibition. The compound occurs 78 times in 65 allowlisted texts and regularly joins 'keeping and breaking' as a paired field of rule judgment. An instruction for beginners requires knowing keeping, breaking, permission, and prohibition, and says to follow the Buddha's words rather than common talk. A Vinaya-master description likewise says such a teacher penetrates keeping and breaking and understands permission and prohibition. Chan polemic turns on the same pair: Zhongfeng quotes claims that embracing a wife, abusing Shakyamuni, drunkenness, and striking Maitreya make discussion of permission, prohibition, keeping, and breaking needless, then interrupts, 'Stop, stop.' A following verse instead says investigating Chan must not destroy or transgress and permission and prohibition must not be confused. Yulin gives an institutional application: because uncovered heads show respect in India whereas full dress shows respect in China, the regulations preserve permission and prohibition while accommodating local custom. The term thus marks real rule-bound distinctions that Chan authors criticize others for discarding and also apply to circumstances.
Senses.Note: No single list of permissions and prohibitions is asserted by this entry; the record uses the compound as a category of precept judgment and repeatedly pairs it with keeping/breaking.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫初心之人。須遠離惡友親近賢善。受五戒十戒等。善知持犯開遮。但依金口聖言。莫順庸流妄說。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An instruction for beginners places permission/prohibition beside keeping/breaking and the reception of five or ten precepts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夫律師者啟毗尼之法藏傳壽命之遺風洞持犯而達開遮秉威儀
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A description of a Vinaya master lists understanding permission and prohibition as part of the office.

Occurrences.Kwic: 叅禪莫毀犯動輙成過患作止誠可分開遮豈容濫內外絕安排自他俱了辨
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A verse says investigating Chan must not transgress and that permission and prohibition cannot be confused.

Occurrences.Kwic: 抱妻罵釋迦。醉酒打彌勒。俱成一行三昧。說甚麼開遮持犯等。故永嘉亦云。大悟不拘於小節。闢曰。且住且住。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng quotes the claimed abolition of permission/prohibition and keeping/breaking, then explicitly interrupts it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 西竺以露頂跣足表至敬東土以冠履備整顯極恭然禮隨國制所行便為虔敬之儀又云葢律依西制結集時仍列開遮宜隨國風以護譏嫌
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yulin applies permission/prohibition to differing Indian and Chinese signs of respect while retaining the authority of the regulations.
